t: The publications of the Bureau of Mines shall be published in editions recommended by the Secretary of the Interior, out not to exceed ten thousand copies for the first edition. When the edition of a publication of the Bureau of Mines is exhausted and the demand for it continues, there may be published, on the requisition of the Secretary of the Interior, as many additional copies as the Secretary of the Interior considers necessary to meet the demand.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that public "demand" for publications brings outsiders into the decision, but demand is only a factual trigger for printing more copies, not consultation, comment, a hearing or a right to sue. Every decision in this section (edition size, additional copies) is made by the Secretary of the Interior, a federal official, with no outside party consulted. No rulemaking, advisory body or coordination with non-federal entities is involved.
fable.s: there may be published, on the requisition of the Secretary of the Interior, as many additional copies as the Secretary of the Interior considers necessary to meet the demand

qwen_block.w: This section describes the internal administrative process for determining the print run of government publications. The decision is made by the Secretary of the Interior, a federal official, based on recommendations (likely from within the agency or based on demand data). There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any party outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. The mention of 'demand' refers to market interest, not a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: The publications of the Bureau of Mines shall be published in editions recommended by the Secretary of the Interior, out not to exceed ten thousand copies for the first edition.

opus.w: This section only sets print-run rules for Bureau of Mines publications, and those decisions stay entirely with the Secretary of the Interior. It might look like public demand gives outsiders a say. But continued demand is only a condition the Secretary weighs, not any consultation, hearing, comment period or advisory process with people outside the government. Every actor involved is inside the federal government.
opus.s: When the edition of a publication of the Bureau of Mines is exhausted and the demand for it continues, there may be published, on the requisition of the Secretary of the Interior, as many additional copies as the Secretary of the Interior considers necessary to meet the demand.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes internal administrative procedures for the publication of government documents. The decisions regarding the number of copies are made by the Secretary of the Interior based on his own judgment of demand, without any requirement for consultation with or participation from outside parties. All actors mentioned (Bureau of Mines, Secretary of the Interior) are within the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: The publications of the Bureau of Mines shall be published in editions recommended by the Secretary of the Interior, out not to exceed ten thousand copies for the first edition. When the edition of a publication of the Bureau of Mines is exhausted and the demand for it continues, there may be published, on the requisition of the Secretary of the Interior, as many additional copies as the Secretary of the Interior considers necessary to meet the demand.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "demand" implies public interest or that the Bureau of Mines interacts with the public. However, the text only describes internal administrative procedures for printing publications based on the Secretary's judgment and requisition. There is no mechanism for the public to participate in the decision of how many copies to print or what to publish. The actors involved are the Bureau of Mines and the Secretary of the Interior, both inside the federal government.
